title: Twelve questions and Karasuno hands you a jersey
dek: Not a quiz about who you'd date on the team. Twelve questions about how you actually behave when the ball's coming at your face and someone has to do something.

questions.prompt: The first thing you do walking into a gym:

options.label: Count who's here and work out who's in charge
Find a ball and start hitting it
Watch where the ball keeps landing
Stand at the back and watch one rally first

questions.prompt: The point that decides the set:

options.label: You want it. You take it, badly if necessary
One serve, no warm-up, all in
You've already quietly updated the rotation
You watch from the side and learn the whole thing

questions.prompt: A teammate is having a genuinely terrible day:

options.label: You quietly give them easier balls
You get loud and carry the energy for both of you
You take the hit that was going to be theirs
You tell them one true, useful thing
You stay after everyone's gone
You over-analyse one mistake for a week
You archive everything and say nothing
You assume you won't be picked
You've already reset the drill
You dive for the one nobody else will
You ask for the ball
You do it properly or you don't do it

questions.prompt: After a loss, the first hour:

options.label: You want the next game immediately
You rewatch it alone and find the exact moment
You say one thing at the right time and it lands
You write it down and don't mention it

questions.prompt: Your role in the group chat:

options.label: Times, addresses, who's bringing the ball
The one who names the elephant
One message that fixes the entire mood
You read everything and reply in three days

questions.prompt: The thing you'd never admit out loud:

options.label: I want to be the one it depends on
I'd take the fall for the whole team
I'm better when nobody's watching me
I'm not sure I belong here yet

questions.prompt: The ball's coming at your face. Instinct:

options.label: Hands up, absorb it
Turn and take it on the back
The reason the play worked
The reason it didn't fall apart

questions.prompt: I'd rather take one high-risk shot than five safe ones.
I need people to know exactly how much I did.

results.name: The Setter
results.tagline: Runs the whole thing without raising their voice
results.blurb: You read the room before the rally. You know who's tired, who's hot and who needs one easy ball to feel alive again, and you arrange all of it so it looks accidental. Your name is rarely on the point. The point doesn't happen without you.
results.watchOut: You can arrange a whole match and still never say what you want. Take one shot yourself.

results.name: The Ace
results.tagline: Wants the ball when it matters
results.blurb: You're not the loudest by accident — you want the last point and you're willing to be the one who misses it. That's rarer than it sounds. When it works, everyone remembers. When it doesn't, you're already asking for the next one.
results.watchOut: Not every ball is yours. A team that only functions when you're on is a fragile team.

results.name: The Libero
results.blurb: You do the job that doesn't show up in the highlights and get weirdly annoyed when someone thanks you for it. You're the reason a bad set became a good rally. You'd rather the save be invisible than have the room look at you.
results.watchOut: Being unsung is a choice you're allowed to stop making. Say what you need once.

results.name: The Middle Blocker
results.blurb: You spend most of the rally waiting and reading, and then you're exactly where the ball is. People mistake your quiet for not caring. You care so much you've been studying the same pattern for weeks, and it pays off in one clean second.
results.watchOut: Waiting can turn into avoiding. Say the thing before the season ends.

results.name: The Wing Spiker
results.blurb: You're the one who changes the temperature of a game. Loud, fast, committed, occasionally wrong about the angle. Your energy is contagious in both directions, which is why the team needs you near the front and sometimes needs you to breathe.
strengths: Changes the mood of a room
results.watchOut: Momentum isn't a plan. One calm decision in the middle of the rush.

results.name: The Pinch Server
results.blurb: You're at your best in the small, high-stakes window: two minutes, one job, everyone watching. You don't need the whole match. You need one chance with consequences, and you'll take the risky version every time.
results.watchOut: The safe serve wins matches too. Not everything needs to be the highlight.

results.name: The Manager
results.blurb: You're the reason there's water, a plan and someone remembering the second-years exist. None of it is glamorous and all of it is load-bearing. You notice who's been quiet for three days before anyone else does.
strengths: Notices people who aren't being noticed
results.watchOut: Nobody's asking you to be the adult every single time. Let someone else carry the water.

results.name: The Bench
results.tagline: Learning the whole thing from the side
results.blurb: You watch everything and say nothing, and then one day you're ready and it surprises people who assumed you weren't paying attention. You're not lesser for not being on court yet. You're just early in a longer story.
results.watchOut: Waiting for a perfect moment is how good players stay on the bench. Ask to play.
